chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Ziyad ibn Suqah, from Al-Hakam ibn 'Utaybah, who said:

I asked Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام about the fingers of the two hands and the fingers of the two feet: What do you say about what exceeds ten fingers and what is less than ten fingers—does it carry a diyah?

He said, and said to me: “O Hakam, the physical form upon which the diyah has been apportioned is ten fingers in the two hands. So whatever exceeds that or falls short of that has no diyah. For each finger from the fingers of the two hands there is one thousand dirhams, and for each finger from the fingers of the two feet there is one thousand dirhams. And everything involving paralysis is assessed at one-third of the diyah of the sound limbs.”

key_terms.أَصَابِعِ: fingers, referring to the digits of the hands and feet in diyah calculations
key_terms.اَلثُّلُثِ: one-third, the legal proportion applied to paralysis compensation
key_terms.اَلصِّحَاحِ: healthy or sound limbs, used as the basis of comparison
key_terms.اَلْخِلْقَةُ: the standard physical creation or natural bodily form recognized in law
key_terms.دِرْهَمٍ: dirham, the monetary unit used to quantify diyah here
key_terms.دِيَةٌ: financial compensation due for bodily injury
key_terms.شَلَلٍ: paralysis or disabling loss of function

ai.seo_question: What is the diyah for fingers of the hands and feet, and is there compensation for extra or missing fingers?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on diyah for the fingers of the hands and feet. It states that compensation is calculated based on the standard created number of ten fingers, assigning one thousand dirhams for each finger of the hands and feet, while extra or missing fingers beyond that standard carry no diyah, and paralysis is assessed at one-third of the diyah of healthy limbs.
